q: In the network 192.168.1.0/24, what is the last usable host address?
explain: .0 is the network address and .255 is the broadcast address, so the last usable host is .254.

q: Which transmission type delivers one packet to every host on the local subnet?
explain: Broadcast is one-to-all within a subnet. ARP and DHCP discovery rely on it in IPv4.

q: OSPF routers exchange updates using 224.0.0.5. What transmission type is that?
explain: 224.0.0.0–239.255.255.255 is the Class D multicast range: one sender, a group of interested receivers.

q: A workstation downloads a file from one web server. Which transmission type is that?
explain: Unicast is one-to-one, the ordinary conversation between two hosts.

q: Why can the first address in a subnet not be assigned to a host?
opts: It is the network address, which identifies the subnet itself
It is reserved for the default gateway
explain: All host bits set to 0 names the network. All host bits set to 1 is the broadcast. Neither can be a host.
